newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch say consensus economy way forward for Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say consensus economy way forward for Europe.

text.p: The consensus style of the Dutch economy could offer important pointers to the way forward for European social policy, Dutch Employment Minister Ad Melkert said on Thursday.

"The strength of the European currency will particularly be determined by the extent to which Europe succeeds in adjusting and readusting...from polarity in industrial relations to institutionalised partnership," he told a three-day conference on European social policy and economic performance.

The Dutch coalition government, led by Melkert's Labour (PvdA) party, currently holds the six-month presidency of the European Union which is grappling with average 11 percent registered unemployment across the 15-nation EU.
In the Netherlands, a set of agreements reached 15 years ago between trade unions and employers had set the stage for the recovery of the Dutch economy, Melkert said.
Such agreements had steered a middle path between the U.S./British model of the free market and the extensive regulation of Germany, Melkert said.
"Traditional institutions (organisations of employers and workers) can play an effective role...when they are prepared to put the common interest above their own," Melkert said.
Governments would have to take such institutions seriously, accepting "employers and workers as participants in the discussion on the design of socio-economic policy," Melkert said.
"In my opinion, this should be the focal point in the modernization of the social dialogue on the European level."
